logs: Review of jobs-b: Pass with five minor findings and no blocker or major. gates/cmd_env.py follows plan section 3 in behaviour: both commands register through S1's COMMANDS with needs="initialised" and no output; env start requires --subject; env stop takes no option, so --subject on it exits 2; each adapter reads the caller once, through vsdd.state.callers.caller(inv.caller_key, project=inv.root), imported inside the function; a malformed subject's ValueError becomes Refuse, exit 2; the dispatcher's --wait is accepted and ignored; the handlers' output and exit codes pass through unchanged. The only interface difference is the names: the plan says run_start, run_stop, configure_start and configure_stop, and the code has the same names with a leading underscore. The builder did not report this. It is rated minor rather than major because no other unit can reach these functions (registration goes through COMMANDS only) and every S1 and records cmd_ module uses the same private-name convention. Both entries marked fixed hold up. AU-S2-12: env-stop.md now gives one syntax, none of the files the finding names still carries commentary, and in a scratch copy test_cli_env_stop_rejects_subject fails when env stop is given a --subject option. P3SEAM-20: in a scratch copy test_cli_env_commands fails when the dispatcher's global --wait is removed, and when env start defines a --wait of its own. The builder was right to leave step3-jobs-fix-4-C2-1 and C2-2 alone: the orchestrator had already marked them left-for-builder, and they are races inside env.py, a file this unit does not own. Six more scratch-copy mutations were each caught by a test: terminal always true, terminal always false, needs changed to mounted, the start ignoring the caller, the stop ignoring the caller, and the Refuse conversion removed. The findings: (1) the launcher test inherits pytest's standard input, so under `pytest -s` in a terminal the marked stop passes even if run_stop drops the marker (shown under a pseudo-terminal); (2) env stop's terminal test ignores VSDD_CALLER, which require_person does not; (3) the unreported function-name difference; (4) env-start.md, unlike the env-stop.md this unit updated, names no failure case; (5) the last assertion in test_start_bad_subject_exits_2 cannot fail. Nothing in the command layer holds state, so a kill at any point leaves nothing partial. The code uses only the standard library and adds no shell. The foreign failure the builder reported has cleared: rewrite/findings/outcomes/step3-hook-runner-fix-5-2.json now parses, and findings.py build succeeds.
